# Chicago Education Digest
_Aug 24 – Sep 07, 2026_

> Covering: K-12 Education & Schools · Board of Education & Governance

## K-12 Curriculum & Instruction

Recent reports from Chicago Public Schools primarily highlight operational adjustments and governance matters, rather than direct developments in K-12 curriculum or instructional methods. A significant theme this past week involved the district's response to extreme weather conditions. Chicago Public Schools initially canceled all outdoor activities due to an extreme heat warning, prioritizing student safety. Following the lifting of this warning, the district subsequently reinstated outdoor activities. These actions reflect CPS's operational decisions in managing school environments during adverse weather.

Separately, news emerged regarding school governance, specifically concerning the upcoming election for the first elected CPS board president. An incumbent school board member, Jennifer Custer, announced her decision to withdraw from the race. This development pertains to the evolving leadership structure of the Chicago Public Schools board.

Overall, the provided news focuses on immediate operational responses to environmental factors affecting school activities and shifts in school board election dynamics. Direct updates or changes related to K-12 curriculum content, instructional strategies, or pedagogical approaches were not a central theme in these reports.

## Students & School Life

Recent reports highlight Chicago Public Schools' ongoing efforts to support student well-being and access, alongside significant developments in district policy and finance. The city has extended a program providing free home internet access to approximately 28,000 CPS students, aiming to ensure digital equity. Additionally, CPS has introduced a new policy designed to simplify enrollment and support services for students experiencing homelessness. Student safety was also a focus, with CPS issuing orders for students to remain indoors during a recent extreme heat warning.

The district continues to address its financial landscape, with budget concerns noted as students began the new school year. In a positive development, CPS successfully recovered millions in federal grants that had been withheld in connection with its Black Student Success Plan. However, the district's policies supporting transgender students are currently under investigation by a House of Representatives committee, indicating potential federal scrutiny of local student support frameworks. Separately, a long-standing case of alleged misconduct by a former CPS teacher from decades ago has seen a development with DNA confirming paternity of a student's child.

## Budget & Finance

Chicago Public Schools (CPS) recently secured millions in federal funding following a lawsuit settlement. The district had challenged the withholding of federal grants, specifically those related to its Black Student Success Plan. This resolution marks a significant financial development for CPS, recovering funds that had been in dispute.

Despite this recovery of federal funds, reports indicate that the district continues to navigate broader budget challenges. As students began the new school year, discussions around CPS's overall financial health and resource allocation remain a key focus for stakeholders.

## Board of Education & Governance

The upcoming election for Chicago's first elected school board president is a prominent theme, with candidates actively campaigning and participating in forums to present their visions. One notable development in the race is the withdrawal of incumbent board member Jennifer Custer. Candidates are also facing scrutiny regarding their backgrounds and past actions, including questions raised about Jessica Biggs' do-not-hire appeal and Victor Henderson's responses to past abuse allegations. Emerging policy discussions among candidates include pledges by some to push for a three-year ban on Artificial Intelligence in schools.

Concurrently, the current Chicago Board of Education recently convened for its first meeting since the start of the school year, with budget concerns remaining a key topic. The district has also implemented new policies, including an extreme heat policy in response to current weather conditions and a policy designed to streamline enrollment and support services for students experiencing homelessness. These actions reflect the ongoing operational responsibilities and policy adjustments within Chicago Public Schools as the city prepares for the transition to an elected school board.

## Equity & Civil Rights

Recent developments in Chicago Public Schools highlight ongoing discussions and actions related to equity and civil rights, particularly concerning student support and federal oversight. A House of Representatives committee has initiated an investigation into the legality of CPS policies designed to support transgender students, signaling federal scrutiny of local district practices in this area. Concurrently, CPS successfully regained millions in federal grants that had been withheld in connection with its Black Student Success Plan, indicating progress in addressing racial equity initiatives and meeting federal compliance requirements.

In related news concerning the district's evolving governance, incumbent school board member Jennifer Custer withdrew from the race to become the first elected CPS board president. This development is part of the broader transition to an elected school board, a change that will significantly influence how future equity and civil rights policies are developed and overseen within the district.
